pages.text: One special Friday Yusuf’s father gets dressed before a flicker of light brightens the sky. He pulls on his heavy weather-proof jacket and the green woollen cap that covers his ears. He waves his boy goodbye. Yusuf’s eyes brighten when Papa says, “Today is the day I will catch a fish and bring a gift home for you.”
pages.alt: Yusuf and Papa high-five each other.
pages.note: Publisher text/alt checked against acquired art. Wordless pages have no inferred story.

pages.text: A fish and a gift? Oh, what will it be? Papa cycles down to Muizenberg Beach. Squeak squeak go the wheels all the way to Surfer’s Corner. Gulls circle the sky. “Whaaat? Whaaat? Whaaat?” they cry. “What will you bring back for Yusuf?” Papa rings his bell. “Wait and see what it will be!”
pages.alt: Papa rides to the beach on his bicycle.
pages.note: Publisher text/alt checked against acquired art. Wordless pages have no inferred story.

pages.text: The fishermen watch the sun rise. They check their nets. They check their oars. They listen to the wind. They drag their boats down to the water. Yusuf’s grandfather, Oupa Salie was a treknet fisherman. Before him his father, Oupagrootjie Ridwaan, knew the sea too.
pages.alt: Papa waves to the fishermen, who prepare to go to sea.
pages.note: Publisher text/alt checked against acquired art. Wordless pages have no inferred story.

pages.text: The boat rides into the waves. Papa’s arms stretch to the oar. His leg braces against the side. His neck strains, his back muscles ripple. Papa sings as he works: “Drop and swish. Find a fish. Pull and plop. Don’t you stop.”
pages.alt: Papa heads out to sea with the other fishermen.
pages.note: Publisher text/alt checked against acquired art. Wordless pages have no inferred story.

pages.text: All day long Yusuf looks at the sky. It is bright and clear and windless. A fish and a gift! What will Papa bring home from the sea? Sometimes he brings a beautiful shell. Sometimes he brings a jewel green bottle rinsed by the waves.
pages.alt: Yusuf examines the gifts Papa has brought him.
pages.note: Publisher text/alt checked against acquired art. Wordless pages have no inferred story.

pages.text: Some days Yusuf’s father brings a story. Like the time they found sea turtles on the sand, hundreds washed up in a storm. “Whaaat? Whaaat? Whaaat?” cried the gulls. “What will you do to help the turtles?” Papa said, “We saved those turtles, I tell you straight. We sent them back to the ocean, every last one.”
pages.alt: Papa stands on the beach with the turtles.
pages.note: Publisher text/alt checked against acquired art. Wordless pages have no inferred story.

pages.text: Always Papa brings a song. He sings the song while he pulls the oars. He sings the song while he pulls the nets. He sings the song as he winds the ropes. He sings the song as he cycles home. “Drop and swish. Find a fish. Pull and plop. Don’t you stop.”
pages.note: Publisher text/alt checked against acquired art. Wordless pages have no inferred story.

pages.text: Ouma Safiya wants a nice fat yellowtail for her supper. Mother wants a new dress. “Don’t be silly,” says Ouma. “You’ll be lucky if they catch even a tiny crab. More likely it will be fish tail Friday. There’s not so many fish left in the sea.” Yusuf holds Ouma’s hand. They cross the road at the bathing cabins. “Whaaat? Whaaat? Whaaat?” cry the gulls perched on the bright rooftops. “What is for supper?”
pages.alt: Ouma Safiya and Yusuf walk to greet Papa.
pages.note: Publisher text/alt checked against acquired art. Wordless pages have no inferred story.

pages.text: Last year the fishermen fought with the surfers. Angry fists and shouting words. “Whaaat? Whaaat? Whaaat?” cried the gulls. “There’s enough sea for everybody,” said Yusuf’s father. He showed them the fishing licence that had been Oupa Salie’s. “Waves for all. Water for free.”
pages.alt: Papa confronts a surfer on the beach.
pages.note: Publisher alt text checked against acquired art; story text is distinct from the image description. Tiny writing in the fishing-licence drawing is not legible text.

pages.text: Ouma Safiya watches through her binoculars, her fingers curled in curiosity. The shark siren sounds. Swimmers run back to the sand and grab their towels. Surfers rush to the shore, carrying their boards under their arms. Under the showers they strip off their wetsuits. “Whaaat? Whaaat? Whaaat?” cry the gulls. “What will Yusuf’s father bring from the ocean?”
pages.alt: Ouma Safiya and Yusuf wait for Papa on the beach. Ouma Safiya looks through her binoculars.
pages.note: Publisher text/alt checked against acquired art. Wordless pages have no inferred story.

pages.text: Yusuf’s father and uncle and cousins heave and pull. A little shark has been caught. It twists and thrashes in the waves. Yusuf’s father untangles the nets, singing to the shark: “Drop and swish. Find a fish. Pull and plop. Don’t you stop.” When the shark at last is free it streaks back into the waves, leaving only one fat yellowtail in the net. Ouma Safiya will be pleased.
pages.alt: Papa finds a shark in the net.
pages.note: Publisher text/alt checked against acquired art. Wordless pages have no inferred story.

pages.text: The men pull the boat in and coil up the cables. A hard white triangle catches Papa’s finger. “Whaaat? Whaaat? Whaaat?” cry the gulls. “What did you bring back for Yusuf?” As the sun goes down, Papa answers the gulls. “A lucky shark tooth for my boy.” At home Yusuf holds his gift up to the stars.
pages.alt: Papa's gift to Yusuf is a shark's tooth.
